articles.title: Game of the Week: Petalburg’s lead meets Rustboro’s renewed offense
articles.dek: The Pride visit the Stone with one more win, two important new absences, and the rest of Hoenn West playing its own consequential game.
articles.author: tessa-wren

body.text: Petalburg brings ten wins to Rustboro. The Stone bring nine, a productive response to a heavy defeat, and the chance to make the division leader spend the final week looking sideways at the standings. Dewford and Mauville meet elsewhere in Hoenn West, so all four clubs will be directly involved in the afternoon’s argument. A division that looked comfortable for the Pride now offers two games worth keeping on the same screen.

My pick is Rustboro 27, Petalburg 20. Shawn Watzon completed twenty-four of thirty-one passes for 263 yards against Canalave, and Philly Gabite added eighty-four rushing yards and two touchdowns. That gives the Stone two credible ways to move the ball. Petalburg has to replace Seviper, its forty-nine-catch tight end, after a one-week injury report. Rustboro has its own serious absence: cornerback Milotic is out for six reported weeks. Neither staff gets to prepare only its strongest version of the team.
Four playoff contenders make this a consequential division round

Petalburg is 10–5. Rustboro and Dewford are 9–6, and Mauville is 8–7. The current playoff table places the Pride third in the conference, the Stone fifth, the Breakers sixth and the Dynamos seventh. Those are the present positions, with two games left for each team. A win here changes the records and the available routes; the separate Playoff Race feature sets out the verified clinching combinations and tiebreak conditions.

A Rustboro victory brings both participants to ten wins and leaves the division open. A Petalburg victory clinches Hoenn West, whatever Dewford does. A tie secures Rustboro a playoff berth and gives Petalburg the division if Dewford ties or loses against Mauville. The Breakers remain title contenders; the Dynamos can affect the title race while pursuing a wild-card berth of their own.

The teams have reached this point in different moods. Petalburg followed a 55–0 loss at Mossdeep with a one-point win at Pastoria, then lost 20–14 to Eterna. Rustboro beat Fortree 29–23, lost 41–7 at Sunyshore and recovered with a 32–14 win over Canalave. Neither three-game sequence establishes a consistently strong contender. Rustboro’s most recent offensive work gives it the better immediate foundation, which is why I favor the home team.
Watzon can make the rush defend the whole field

Watzon’s Canalave performance matters beyond the final passing total. Completing twenty-four of thirty-one means he kept finding usable throws without needing a spectacular gain on every attempt. He threw two touchdown passes and no interceptions. His season line now stands at twelve touchdown passes against two interceptions, with 1,648 passing yards. The Stone have a passer who has generally protected the ball while still producing enough to support the running game.

Petalburg has thirty sacks this season. That is a credible defensive answer, especially against an offense whose passing can become much less comfortable when it falls behind. Rustboro has allowed eighteen sacks through fifteen games, so the matchup pits a productive rush against a team that has usually avoided large sack totals. My measurable target for the Stone is no more than two sacks allowed. Reaching it would leave Watzon more opportunities to choose among his receivers on ordinary down-and-distance terms.

Gibby Timmy caught two passes for sixty-four yards against Canalave and has 660 receiving yards this season. Gengar added four catches for fifty last week; SEARED BITE caught five for fifty-three. Those are different contributions to a passing game that does not require one receiver to win every possession. Petalburg must prevent the larger gains without making all the shorter completions easy. I expect the Pride to contest the first read more successfully than Canalave did, but Rustboro has shown enough options to answer some of that resistance.

“People want the offense explained like it’s a secret handshake,” Tyler Scarboro said. “If the throw is there, complete it. If they leave you room to run, run. The complicated part is getting eleven people to do the sensible thing at the same time.” That is a fair description of the challenge after a thirty-two-point performance. The sensible choice has to remain available when Petalburg brings a more productive season pass rush.
Gabite gives the Stone a practical first move

Philly Gabite has 784 rushing yards and ten rushing touchdowns on 166 carries. Against Canalave he gained eighty-four on seventeen attempts and scored twice. Watchog contributed another forty-seven yards and a touchdown on twelve carries. My Way, Son remains unavailable for two reported weeks, but the Stone’s recent ground production demonstrates that the available runners can do meaningful work without him.

Rustboro has 2,099 rushing yards as a team. Petalburg has allowed 1,279, a little more than eighty-five a game. That difference in established production creates the central contest: can the Stone generate useful early gains against a defense that has generally limited rushing totals? If they can, Watzon gets to operate without a string of predictable passing situations. If the Pride repeatedly force short gains, their thirty-sack defense becomes a larger part of the game.

My target for Petalburg is to hold Rustboro below 120 rushing yards. That is an analytical target for this matchup, rather than a claim that a particular total guarantees victory. The Pride also need a positive turnover margin. Watzon’s two season interceptions make that a demanding request, but Petalburg intercepted Tatsugiri twice last week. Producing those chances against a more careful passer would give the visitors a way to offset their missing receiving production.
Petalburg must replace forty-nine catches

Seviper caught five passes for forty-three yards in the loss to Eterna. His season totals are forty-nine receptions, 494 yards and four touchdowns. The new injury report lists one week out, so Petalburg must prepare this game without a major part of its short and intermediate receiving work. A small reported duration can still arrive at a particularly inconvenient place on the schedule.

Farigiraf has twenty-four catches for 416 yards and four touchdowns this season. His current form follows the confirmed evolution from Girafarig, so the receiving record belongs to the same player throughout that change. He is an established option for more work, though the available report does not announce a replacement assignment. Vikavolt has forty-two receptions for 408 yards. Petalburg has other players who have caught meaningful passes; the question is whether it can arrange those contributions efficiently enough to cover Seviper’s absence.

Iron Valiant threw for 130 yards against Eterna, with one touchdown and one interception. His season line is 2,282 yards, twenty-two touchdowns and ten interceptions. Those totals describe an offense capable of finishing drives, but its recent passing output leaves little margin when the run game struggles. Oinkologne gained thirty-four yards on eleven carries last week. Petalburg needs more useful work from that combination to keep a twenty-seven-point Rustboro forecast from becoming an uncomfortable requirement of its own.

The Pride can test a newly weakened part of the Stone defense. Milotic’s six-week injury report removes a cornerback before a game in which Petalburg badly needs its available receivers to contribute. That does not establish who will take each coverage assignment, and I will not give an unconfirmed replacement a difficult afternoon in advance. It does give Iron Valiant and the receiving group a concrete area to examine as the game develops.
Rustboro needs defensive help beyond sacks

The Stone have sixteen sacks this season, against Petalburg’s thirty. Rustboro cannot assume it will erase a substantial share of the Pride’s possessions with pressure alone. Its defense has allowed 290 points, only fifteen more than Petalburg’s 275, but the recent 41–7 defeat at Sunyshore showed how quickly the margin can expand when an opponent sustains both rushing and passing production.

Petalburg’s best route is therefore fairly specific. Oinkologne needs to turn more first-down carries into manageable second downs, and Iron Valiant must distribute the ball among the remaining established receivers. The Pride can then ask its own pass rush for a few drives that end before Rustboro reaches scoring range. A productive passing afternoon against the Stone’s changed coverage group would matter much more than an abstract demand to respond to last week’s loss.

Rustboro’s route begins with the available backfield, continues through Watzon’s accurate passing and requires enough defensive stops to keep both parts of the offense usable. A narrow early deficit would still leave the Stone room to run. Repeated Petalburg touchdowns would force Watzon into the much harder assignment of answering every possession. That is why the injured cornerback matters even in a preview that favors Rustboro’s offense.
The forecast and the checks

I expect Gabite and Watchog to provide enough rushing support for Watzon to complete at least sixty-five percent of his passes. That is below his Canalave rate and above his season rate, a reasonable target against better pressure with a functioning running game beside him. I also expect Petalburg to produce a more competitive passing total than last week’s 130 yards because Milotic’s absence leaves Rustboro with work to do in coverage.

My 27–20 score gives the Stone four scoring possessions and asks Petalburg to reach twenty points despite losing its most productive receiver by catch total. The alternative I take most seriously is a Pride victory built on pressure and takeaways: three or more sacks, an interception that changes a possession, and enough Oinkologne production to prevent a succession of difficult passing downs. Mara Voss chooses Petalburg on that defensive argument in the panel. I favor Watzon’s recent accuracy and the Stone’s available runners.

The two sideline reports also remain relevant after kickoff. Petalburg needs to show how Seviper’s catches are redistributed, and Rustboro needs a workable answer in Milotic’s part of the defense. Those are observable jobs, and they will tell us more about each team’s next game than a generic declaration of playoff readiness. For this one, I expect Rustboro’s balanced scoring to bring the two clubs level on wins before the final round.

articles.title: Mossdeep secures the bye; six berths remain open
articles.dek: Lavender joins the playoff field, Mt. Silver can finish its bye race at Azalea, and three divisions can be decided in Week 17. Ellis Quill traces the wins, ties and rival results that change the field.
articles.author: ellis-quill

body.text: Mossdeep has earned the first week off. Lavender has earned a place in the postseason. Everyone still chasing an invitation can find a useful lesson in the difference: a team can settle one question while leaving several others worth playing for. The Eclipse are 15–0 after beating Sunyshore 27–3, with the Hoenn–Sinnoh first seed secured. The Wails are 10–5 after winning 32–21 at Cerulean, with a division title still available.

I would expect Michael Dorrill to spend considerably more time on the three points allowed than on the administrative pleasure of a bye. His team has earned the right to prepare without an opening-round opponent. That is an advantage with a precise shape: every Hoenn–Sinnoh challenger must survive an additional game, and any conference playoff game Mossdeep plays will be at home.

Mt. Silver had an opportunity to settle the other bye and lost 38–24 at Cinnabar. Saffron, meanwhile, beat Blackthorn 70–0. The Reds still control their own route, but their margin over the Psi Corps has narrowed to one game. The two remaining regular-season rounds now contain three unsettled divisions, six unclaimed berths, and several games in which both participants can change their postseason position directly.
Eight teams have qualified; Mossdeep owns the only bye

body.title: Secured through Week 16
body.description: Season 1, through Week 16. Future results are conditional where stated.

cells: Z — conference first seed and bye

body.text: Mossdeep’s fifteen wins exceed Sunyshore’s final ceiling of thirteen. Lavender’s guarantee uses the division tiebreak as well as the record. Violet can reach ten wins, but the Wails already have three division victories while the Falcons can finish with only two. If the clubs finish level overall, Lavender stays ahead. There is no remaining allocation of wins, losses and ties that removes the Wails from the seven-team field.

Rustboro, Dewford and Eterna have nine wins each and still need another result. Each has a possible finish outside the field. Their present seeds belong on a standings page; they do not yet earn an X. Seven clubs qualify per conference: four division champions and three wild cards. Division champions receive the first four seeds, and only the first seed receives a bye.
Mt. Silver can settle the bye at Azalea

A Mt. Silver victory at Azalea clinches the Kanto–Johto first seed. The Reds would reach fourteen wins. Saffron could match fourteen only by winning twice, and Mt. Silver owns the head-to-head victory from Week 15. Blackthorn can finish with no more than thirteen wins. The Reds can complete this job without waiting for either rival.

A tie at Azalea is enough if Saffron ties or loses at Cerulean. If the Reds lose, they need both a Saffron loss and a Blackthorn tie or loss at Mahogany. These are complete Week 17 bye routes. Every other combination leaves at least one possible final-week finish in which Mt. Silver loses the first seed.

body.title: Week 17: Mt. Silver’s complete bye routes
body.description: Follow the Reds’ result first. A branch marked open preserves at least one rival route; it does not award the bye to that rival.

body.text: Saffron’s remaining schedule is Cerulean away and Fuchsia at home; Mt. Silver finishes with Cianwood at home after Azalea. A straightforward Psi Corps route is to win twice while the Reds lose twice. That would give Saffron fourteen wins and Mt. Silver thirteen, making their earlier head-to-head result irrelevant. A head-to-head advantage breaks an equal-record argument; it cannot supply a missing win.

The Reds’ injury report gives the bye additional practical value. Tic Thorpe still has five weeks reported, Josh Alakazam six, and Ariados now has twelve after the Cinnabar game. None of those counters promises a return by a particular playoff round. The immediate football task belongs to the available players, and an earned bye would remove one game from that task.
Three divisions can be decided in Week 17

body.text: Blackthorn still leads Lavender by one game after the 70–0 defeat. Their Week 18 meeting in Lavender is the reason a division race survives that gap. The Wails can keep their title route alive by winning at Violet, whatever Blackthorn does at Mahogany. If both contenders win, the final meeting decides the division: a Lavender win produces matching 12–5 records and gives the Wails the superior division record after a split head-to-head series; a Blackthorn win or tie preserves the Dragons’ lead.

Petalburg’s 20–14 loss to Eterna brings Rustboro within one game just before their meeting. A Pride victory settles Hoenn West immediately. A Rustboro victory leaves the division open and makes the final round—Dewford at Rustboro and Mauville at Petalburg—essential viewing. The Stone can qualify with a tie, yet a tied game can simultaneously give Petalburg the division if Dewford fails to win. The same result can be a useful achievement for one sideline and an incomplete job for the other.

The table deliberately leaves deeper combinations unclassified when they require additional tiebreak analysis; an unlisted result is not an elimination notice. Mauville’s row requires its own victory. A club on eight wins cannot simply borrow the clinching arithmetic of its nine-win neighbors.

Olivine and Vermilion have an obvious reason to watch Lavender at Violet. Both are 8–7 alongside the Falcons. A Lavender victory prevents Violet from reaching ten wins and gives the other contenders room to finish their qualification arguments. Olivine’s 19–0 win over Vermilion in Week 15 remains valuable when those clubs finish level. The Ironclads now report Magmar out for two weeks and Bibarel for one, however, so their immediate task against Cianwood comes with new absences.

Dewford–Mauville is unusually direct. A Dewford win or tie secures the Breakers’ place. A Mauville win puts the Dynamos on nine victories and brings the listed help routes into play. Dewford then travels to Rustboro, while Mauville visits Petalburg. Neither club can arrange a quiet last fortnight by looking past its divisional neighbors.

body.text: When Olivine and Vermilion both win their finales in this setup, they qualify with Lavender and Violet misses at 10–7. If Vermilion wins while Olivine ties or loses, Violet replaces the Ironclads. If Vermilion ties while Olivine loses, Violet and Vermilion get the remaining places. A tie in both games sends Violet and Olivine through: the Ironclads’ head-to-head win settles their 9–7–1 comparison with the Volts.

A Cerulean win sends Violet through in all three Olivine branches here, with Olivine taking the other place. Cerulean itself finishes no better than 8–9 under the fixed assumptions, because this example includes a Week 17 loss to Saffron. The chart therefore demonstrates the Tide changing another club’s qualification without claiming that Cerulean has already been eliminated from every possible finish.
The present bracket and the next opponents

If the current seeds held, Saffron would host Vermilion, Blackthorn would host Olivine, and Cinnabar would host Lavender. In Hoenn–Sinnoh, Sunyshore would host Mauville, Petalburg would host Dewford, and Eterna would host Rustboro. Mt. Silver occupies the Kanto–Johto bye position today; Mossdeep has secured the Hoenn–Sinnoh bye. Those six opening-round pairings remain provisional.

Mossdeep finishes against Sootopolis at home and Lavaridge away. Sunyshore travels to Pastoria and Veilstone. Lavender still has People Eater listed for one week and Mr. Clanky for seven while it visits Violet and prepares to host Blackthorn. Rustboro has a new six-week absence for Milotic before consecutive home games against Petalburg and Dewford. The remaining fixtures are short enough to list, and consequential enough that every contender should know which other scoreboard belongs beside its own.

articles.dek: Petalburg–Rustboro leads a sixteen-game slate; Mauville tests Dewford, Lavender visits Violet, and eighty writer picks cover every matchup.
articles.author: tessa-wren

body.text: Hoenn West supplies the two games I most want to watch. Petalburg visits Rustboro with a one-win lead over the Stone, while Dewford hosts a Mauville team that has won three straight. Lavender goes to Violet in a matchup between a ten-win club and an eight-win team currently outside the playoff seeds. Saffron and Mt. Silver continue the chase at the top of Kanto–Johto against very different opponents.

I went 11–5 last week. My Mossdeep–Sunyshore forecast, 38–21, gave both offenses too much credit: the Eclipse won 27–3. Mossdeep met both of my slate targets: it allowed two sacks and held Sunyshore to three conversions in ten third downs. The Starseekers met the limit of four passing touchdowns allowed, conceding two, but missed the target of 120 rushing yards with forty-eight. I expect Sunyshore to respond at Pastoria, but a response has to show up in completed passes before it earns a new reputation.

All sixteen games appear below with checkable targets and my own score forecast. Each panelist chose a separate score and argument; the picks are editorial judgments, not playoff odds or promises about game outcomes.

matchups.matchup: A modest passing target in a low-scoring game
matchups.analysis: Viridian beat Cianwood with 104 passing yards from Mr. Rime and 84 rushing yards from Gabite. Pewter produced five sacks against Olivine but lost despite holding the visitors to twelve points. I expect another game in which one clean touchdown drive matters more than a large yardage total.
matchups.awayKey: Complete at least half the passes and throw no interceptions.
matchups.homeKey: Rush for at least ninety yards and allow no more than two sacks.

matchups.matchup: Cinnabar needs new runners around a thriving passer
matchups.analysis: Gholdengo completed 33 of 41 passes for 357 yards against Mt. Silver. Arcanine, who contributed two rushing touchdowns and fifty receiving yards, now has a three-week injury report; Seismitoad remains out one. Celadon shut out Azalea, but its own hundred passing yards leave a considerable scoring gap to bridge.
matchups.awayKey: Complete at least sixty-five percent of passes and lose no more than one turnover.
matchups.homeKey: Hold Cinnabar below twenty-four points and reach 150 rushing yards.

matchups.matchup: Cerulean must survive the pass rush
matchups.analysis: Saffron has sixty-nine sacks through fifteen games, including seven by NeMarcus Tare against Blackthorn. Archam Manning added 528 passing yards and seven touchdowns in the 70–0 win. Cerulean can move the ball through Zebstrika, but Farigiraf threw two interceptions against Lavender.
matchups.awayKey: Record at least four sacks and throw no interceptions.
matchups.homeKey: Allow no more than two sacks and complete three passes gaining twenty yards or more.

matchups.matchup: Vermilion can lean on Kangaskhan again
matchups.analysis: Kangaskhan ran for 107 yards and caught a touchdown in the win over Mahogany. Fuchsia made Violet work in a 20–17 loss, with Empoleon throwing no interceptions, but the Shadows have conceded 321 points this season. Vermilion needs another controlled offensive game to defend its current seventh seed.
matchups.awayKey: Throw no interceptions and hold Kangaskhan below eighty rushing yards.
matchups.homeKey: Rush for at least one hundred yards and limit turnovers to one.

matchups.matchup: Mt. Silver can restore the running emphasis
matchups.analysis: Garshawn Lynch gained 113 yards on eight carries and scored three total touchdowns at Cinnabar. Jacoby Brizzet did most of the passing in that loss; Tic Thorpe and Josh Alakazam remain unavailable, and Ariados now has twelve reported weeks out. Azalea has allowed 1,958 rushing yards, the largest total in the league.
matchups.awayKey: Rush for at least 150 yards and give the ball away no more than once.
matchups.homeKey: Hold Lynch below one hundred yards and score on three possessions.

matchups.matchup: Two limited passing attacks put a premium on finishing
matchups.analysis: Olivine has won twice while allowing ten total points. New injuries to Magmar and Bibarel complicate a receiving group that already lacked Stantler and Beedrill, although Maractus and Thievul have cleared their positive recovery counters. Cianwood managed three points at Viridian; Gardevoir still has one reported week out.
matchups.awayKey: Rush for at least 120 yards and score two offensive touchdowns.
matchups.homeKey: Allow fewer than fourteen points and throw no more than one interception.

matchups.matchup: Lavender brings its running game to an urgent host
matchups.analysis: Hobbes ran for 122 yards and two touchdowns at Cerulean. Violet answered Fuchsia with 176 passing yards from Iron Jugulis and ninety-six receiving yards from Samurott, but now loses Maractus for two reported weeks. Lavender enters 10–5; Violet is 8–7 and currently outside the seven playoff seeds.
matchups.awayKey: Gain at least 120 rushing yards and allow fewer than three sacks.
matchups.homeKey: Hold Hobbes below eighty rushing yards and score three offensive touchdowns.

matchups.matchup: Blackthorn needs a recovery in protection
matchups.analysis: The Dragons have allowed forty-three sacks and were shut out at Saffron. Sawsbuck now carries a six-week injury report. Mahogany gained 236 passing yards at Vermilion, 174 through Dugtrio, but its run game stalled and safety Frosmoth is newly out nine weeks.
matchups.awayKey: Allow no more than two sacks and score three touchdowns.
matchups.homeKey: Complete three passes gaining twenty yards or more and keep turnovers to one.

matchups.matchup: Hoenn West meets at the line of scrimmage
matchups.analysis: Petalburg leads Rustboro by one win, with Dewford also pursuing the division title and Mauville chasing a wild-card berth. Shawn Watzon completed 24 of 31 against Canalave, and Philly Gabite scored twice. The Pride must replace newly injured Seviper; Rustboro loses cornerback Milotic for six reported weeks. The full Game of the Week feature examines the competing ways to attack those absences.
matchups.awayKey: Hold Rustboro below 120 rushing yards and finish with a positive turnover margin.
matchups.homeKey: Complete at least sixty-five percent of passes and allow no more than two sacks.

matchups.matchup: A direct test of the wild-card order
matchups.analysis: Dewford is 9–6 and Mauville 8–7. Both occupy current playoff seeds. Dewford can still win Hoenn West; Mauville is pursuing a wild-card berth. Mauville has won three straight, most recently 37–0 over Snowpoint; Dewford answered its Hearthome loss with a 24–10 win over Oreburgh. This is the other essential division game on the slate.
matchups.awayKey: Throw no interceptions and hold Dewford below one hundred rushing yards.
matchups.homeKey: Convert at least forty percent of third downs and score three touchdowns.

matchups.matchup: The Inferno can attack a vulnerable defense
matchups.analysis: Delphox threw four touchdowns against Pastoria, three to Fearow. Lavaridge also intercepted five passes. Fortree has allowed 389 points and fifty-two sacks this season, so the Skyhawks must improve at both ends to prevent another difficult road afternoon.
matchups.awayKey: Allow no more than two sacks and hold Fearow below eighty receiving yards.
matchups.homeKey: Complete two touchdown passes and limit turnovers to one.

matchups.matchup: Mossdeep has multiple ways to keep winning
matchups.analysis: The Eclipse held Sunyshore to three points while Poury Holt gained 121 rushing yards and Dram Marino passed for 316. Sootopolis lost 24–18 to Veilstone and still has cornerback Kingdra unavailable for three reported weeks. Mossdeep’s passing depth and running production present more problems than the Surge have recently solved.
matchups.awayKey: Force two turnovers and hold Mossdeep below thirty points.
matchups.homeKey: Complete at least seventy percent of passes and allow fewer than fourteen points.

matchups.matchup: Eterna can ask its defense for another controlled win
matchups.analysis: Eterna held Petalburg to fourteen while Tatsugiri threw two touchdowns and two interceptions. Oreburgh now loses cornerback Dusknoir and receivers Sharpedo and Poliwhirl, adding to a difficult week after the 24–10 defeat at Dewford. The Thorns should have the stronger defensive platform.
matchups.awayKey: Limit interceptions to one and allow fewer than fourteen points.
matchups.homeKey: Force two takeaways and reach one hundred rushing yards.

matchups.matchup: A low-scoring chance to stop a losing run
matchups.analysis: Canalave has lost three straight; Snowpoint has also lost its last three and was shut out by Mauville. Slowking threw for ninety-four yards at Rustboro, so the Bulwark still need improvement even against an opponent struggling to score. Canalave’s season rushing defense supplies the most convincing edge.
matchups.awayKey: Pass for at least 180 yards and lose no more than one turnover.
matchups.homeKey: Hold Snowpoint below eighty rushing yards and score two offensive touchdowns.

matchups.matchup: Hearthome looks for a fourth straight win
matchups.analysis: Frosmoth passed for 253 yards and Feraligatr rushed for 108 at Fortree. Veilstone also won on the road, scoring twenty-four at Sootopolis, but now has Vigoroth out three reported weeks. Hearthome loses cornerback Dodrio for four, leaving a vulnerability for the visitors to test.
matchups.awayKey: Complete at least sixty percent of passes and hold Feraligatr below eighty rushing yards.
matchups.homeKey: Score three touchdowns and throw no interceptions.

matchups.matchup: Sunyshore gets a chance to repair its passing game
matchups.analysis: DeZhaun Watzon threw for 122 yards at Mossdeep after four touchdown passes against Rustboro the week before. Pastoria’s Farigiraf threw five interceptions at Lavaridge. Serp Gardener has cleared his positive recovery counter; that does not by itself establish a starting assignment, but it improves Sunyshore’s availability picture.
matchups.awayKey: Complete at least sixty percent of passes and score three offensive touchdowns.
matchups.homeKey: Throw no more than one interception and hold Sunyshore below one hundred rushing yards.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Viridian just won while scoring twelve, which is positively extravagant in this company. Pewter’s two interceptions make the Titans the safer low-scoring choice.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Pewter generated five sacks against Olivine. I trust that pressure to disrupt Mr. Rime before Viridian’s running game can establish the same control.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Neither offense has earned a generous forecast. Viridian’s eighty-four yards from Gabite offer the slightly steadier way to keep a narrow lead.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: The Rockers have nineteen points across two losses and another pair of interceptions to explain. Viridian can win this without commissioning a monument to offensive football.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Pewter can create pressure, but its passing mistakes give Viridian the better chance to win a game with very few scoring possessions.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Cinnabar has beaten Blackthorn and Mt. Silver in consecutive weeks. Celadon’s shutout earns respect; its hundred passing yards earn a much smaller score prediction.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Arcanine’s absence removes useful receiving and finishing work, but Gholdengo’s distribution against Mt. Silver was excellent. Celadon lacks enough passing production to answer it.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Blaze must redistribute Arcanine’s touches, and Celadon has allowed only seventeen points in two games. I expect a slower win than Cinnabar’s recent headlines suggest.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Thirty-three completions against the Reds are evidence I can use. Cinnabar’s receivers can carry the scoring while the backfield adjusts, and I expect them to do it emphatically.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: The missing backs should reduce Cinnabar’s efficiency near the goal line, but the broad passing attack still offers more scoring opportunities than Celadon has recently created.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: HeeDee Lamb caught five touchdowns last week. Cerulean allowed thirty-two to Lavender, so I expect Saffron’s passing advantage to become visible before halftime.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Cerulean’s deep passing has a chance only if the protection lasts. Saffron’s sixty-nine season sacks persuade me that too many Tide possessions will end before that happens.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Zebstrika’s 134 receiving yards give Cerulean a credible answer on some possessions. Saffron should still win comfortably without reproducing an extraordinary seventy-point afternoon.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Blackthorn arrived with eleven victories and left with seventy unanswered points against it. Cerulean has allowed 321 this season; Saffron will find enough of the same openings.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: I expect Cerulean to produce a few explosive completions, but Saffron’s pressure and Manning’s recent ball security should make the visitors' scoring much more repeatable.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Vermilion has rediscovered touchdowns, a development I welcome with appropriate caution. Kangaskhan’s running should keep the Volts ahead of a Fuchsia attack still short on sustained production.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Volts can give Kangaskhan meaningful early-down work against a defense that has conceded more than 1,300 rushing yards. That reduces the burden on an interception-prone passing game.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Empoleon avoided interceptions against Violet, while Chandelure threw two. I can see Fuchsia winning the possession battle and taking one of these close games at last.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Fuchsia has three wins and keeps finding ways to turn respectable stretches into another loss. Vermilion’s hundred-yard runner supplies a more convincing finishing plan.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Kangaskhan’s production gives Vermilion an advantage, though the Volts' secondary injuries and recent passing mistakes should allow Fuchsia to remain within a score.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Azalea just went scoreless against Celadon and now faces a runner who needed eight carries for 113 yards. Mt. Silver should enjoy this particular change of opponent.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Swarm’s run defense has conceded almost two thousand yards. Mt. Silver can reduce the demands on its replacement passing group and still control the game through Lynch.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Losing Ariados makes a difficult passing situation harder. I still trust the Reds' defense and Lynch to provide a stable response against an offense shut out last week.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: The Reds have a back who scored all three of their touchdowns at Cinnabar. Against Azalea’s run defense, I expect Connor McLarren to keep finding reasons to hand him the ball.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Azalea’s vulnerable rushing defense fits Mt. Silver’s healthiest source of offense. I expect the Reds to win without asking another unsettled passing group to carry the afternoon.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Olivine has conceded ten points in two weeks. Cianwood managed three at Viridian, which is a persuasive argument against expecting an immediate scoring festival.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Olivine’s receiver absences leave too much work for Veluza, and Drampa threw two interceptions at Pewter. Bibarel can give Cianwood enough rushing production to steal a narrow one.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Ironclads keep making a small number of points sufficient. I expect that defensive consistency to survive another week while their receiving rotation changes again.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Cianwood’s passing game produced 127 yards against Viridian. Olivine has already shown it can win this kind of uncomfortable little contest without much offensive assistance.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Olivine’s recent defense deserves the edge, but the new receiving injuries make a comfortable margin unlikely. Cianwood’s ground game should keep the possessions competitive.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Violet has won two straight and gets Lavender’s defense after it allowed 302 passing yards. Samurott can keep the Falcons moving even with Maractus unavailable.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Lavender’s 122 yards from Hobbes gave Frosmoth usable situations against Cerulean. I expect the Wails to keep feeding that advantage while Violet replaces a productive slot option.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Travis Scarboro’s team has won three straight without needing the same offensive formula each week. Hobbes gives Lavender a dependable opening argument on the road.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Lavender’s season point differential remains minus thirty-four despite ten wins. Violet has a productive tight end and a chance to make the Wails defend a much cleaner game.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Hobbes should give Lavender the more stable rushing foundation. Violet can threaten through Samurott, but Maractus’s injury removes another contributor just as the Falcons need a win.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Seventy-zero leaves a bruise on my rankings, but Mahogany does not have Saffron’s pass rush. Blackthorn’s season-long receiving production can still win a less violent matchup.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Dragons' protection problems remain serious, and losing Sawsbuck narrows their choices. Mahogany’s seventeen rushing yards from Exploud keep me from trusting the Frost to exploit every opening.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Dugtrio supplied 174 receiving yards last week. I expect Mahogany to find enough explosive plays while Blackthorn works through a damaged rushing attack and a rough protection stretch.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Blackthorn has nearly four thousand passing yards this season. I expect that offense to reappear against a Frost defense now missing another safety, even if the Dragons remain deeply flawed.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Mahogany should reach Blackthorn through Dugtrio, but its latest rushing output was too limited. The Dragons have the stronger passing record and a more manageable opponent this week.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Rustboro recovered with thirty-two points while Petalburg has thirty-five across three games. Watzon’s accuracy gives the Stone a stronger immediate offensive case than the division leader.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Petalburg has thirty sacks this season and Rustboro only sixteen. I expect the Pride’s pressure to make Watzon less comfortable while Milotic’s absence creates enough receiving room.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Stone have a productive runner and a quarterback coming off an accurate afternoon. Petalburg can keep this close, but Seviper’s absence removes a familiar way to finish difficult possessions.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: A division lead is useful; an offense that has scored fourteen and zero in two of its last three games is concerning. Rustboro has enough balance to punish another slow Pride start.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Watzon’s clean passing and Gabite’s rushing should give Rustboro more reliable scoring possessions. Petalburg’s defense can resist, but losing its forty-nine-catch tight end tips my choice.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Dewford’s Frosmoth completed thirteen of eighteen last week. I like that efficiency against a Mauville defense whose impressive shutout came against a struggling Snowpoint offense.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Volbeat supplied four sacks against Snowpoint. If Mauville brings comparable disruption to Dewford, the Dynamos can take the passing game away from the Breakers' preferred comfortable downs.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Mauville’s three straight wins deserve a serious response. Dewford’s more substantial season rushing production gives the home team a narrow edge in a game I expect to remain close.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Togekiss threw three touchdowns without an interception in a thirty-seven-point win. Mauville has the better current passing rhythm, and I expect it to travel.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Mauville has found productive passing and timely pressure during its winning streak. Dewford’s balanced attack makes this nearly even, but I favor one additional Dynamos finishing drive.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Fearow just caught three touchdowns and Fortree has conceded more points than anyone. Lavaridge should find room without needing another five-interception gift from the opponent.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Fortree’s fifty-two sacks allowed keep sabotaging its scoring chances. Lavaridge can win through pressure and its improving passing game even if the turnover count returns to normal.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Inferno have two straight wins and a productive Delphox–Fearow connection. Fortree can score more than last week’s seven, but its defense asks for too much compensation.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Lavaridge scored thirty-eight against Pastoria, and Fortree just gave Hearthome twenty-seven. Delphox has the right opponent for another conspicuous afternoon.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: I expect Lavaridge’s passing to stay productive against a defense allowing almost twenty-six points a game. Fortree’s protection record makes matching those scores difficult.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Mossdeep allowed Sunyshore three points and found a hundred-yard runner of its own. Sootopolis has neither the scoring consistency nor the healthy coverage group to keep pace.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Poury Holt’s production lets Mossdeep punish a defense that commits too heavily to Marino’s receivers. The Surge also need an answer to a pass rush with fifty-two season sacks.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Mossdeep’s defense has allowed seventeen points across its last three games. I expect another comfortable win, though Sootopolis’s occasional explosive passing should produce a couple of scores.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: The Eclipse handled a real contender last week, which I will acknowledge in writing. Against a six-win Surge team missing Kingdra, their receiving depth should be sufficient again.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Marino completed twenty-one of twenty-six against Sunyshore, and Holt made the running game a genuine scoring source. Sootopolis’s depleted secondary faces too many reliable contributors.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Eterna just won at Petalburg and now gets a three-win opponent with fresh injuries in coverage and at receiver. The Thorns do not need a glamorous offense for this one.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: Eterna has allowed only 845 rushing yards this season. If Oreburgh cannot create a useful ground game, its depleted receiving group must carry too much against a disciplined defense.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: The Thorns can be careless with the ball, as two interceptions at Petalburg showed. Their defense should still make a modest scoring total enough against the injured Miners.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Oreburgh lost two receivers and a cornerback while losing at Dewford. Eterna’s own passing is imperfect, but the matchup supplies several obvious places to make progress.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Eterna’s defense has allowed 171 points through fifteen games. Oreburgh’s new receiving absences make it harder to sustain the drives needed to challenge that unit.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Snowpoint has fifteen points across three losses. Canalave’s offense is hardly a tourist attraction, but its run defense can make the visitors' afternoon even smaller.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Bulwark have allowed only 931 rushing yards this season. That should force Snowpoint’s passing game to create more than its recent hundred-yard afternoons.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Both clubs need a response, and Canalave has scored twenty-one points across three defeats. Snowpoint’s larger season passing total gives me a slight upset lean in an awkward matchup.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Snowpoint went scoreless against Mauville and has allowed thirty-four sacks this season. Canalave should get enough stops to win even with its limited passing offense.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Canalave’s stronger rushing defense should decide a game between two struggling attacks. I expect the Bulwark to make a small improvement on last week’s fourteen points.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Hearthome has three straight wins and just produced a hundred-yard runner plus 253 passing yards. Veilstone’s new Vigoroth absence makes keeping up less straightforward.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Haunts have demonstrated useful balance, which should keep Veilstone from attacking only the pass. Dodrio’s absence leaves enough receiving opportunity for the Fists to make this close.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Hearthome has outscored its last three opponents seventy-three to twenty-six. That sustained improvement deserves more weight than its early-season record when judging this particular matchup.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: Dodrio’s injury gives Veilstone an opening against a defense already missing Mr. Mime. The Fists just scored twenty-four on the road; I expect another productive passing day.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Hearthome’s recent balance earns a narrow pick. Veilstone can exploit the secondary absences, but replacing Vigoroth’s touches makes its own offensive task more complicated.

picks.author: rowan-vale
picks.reason: Pastoria followed a competitive loss with five interceptions and a twenty-eight-point defeat. Sunyshore should recover against an opponent much less capable of shrinking Watzon’s passing game.

picks.author: mara-voss
picks.reason: The Starseekers have allowed only 748 rushing yards this season. If Pastoria must ask Farigiraf for repeated difficult throws, last week’s interception problem becomes especially relevant.

picks.author: ellis-quill
picks.reason: Sunyshore’s offense has been uneven across its last two games. Its much stronger season defense should still give the Starseekers room to recover without needing forty points.

picks.author: dorian-pike
picks.reason: I remain unconvinced by Sunyshore’s offense against elite opposition. Pastoria is a different assignment: five interceptions against Lavaridge give the visitors a very clear route to separation.

picks.author: tessa-wren
picks.reason: Pastoria’s passing mistakes and Sunyshore’s strong rushing defense make this a favorable recovery matchup. I expect Watzon to find his receivers more readily than he did at Mossdeep.
